newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil barges soften.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil barges soften.

text.p: High sulphur cracked fuel oil was steady to weaker in a thin on Wednesday, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $95 a tonne fob ARA for running refinery material, and then at $94 for RMG. around 15,000 tonnes' worth of business was thought to have been done.
High sulphur cargoes were little changed and industry functionsin London also hampered business.

Russian exports continue apace. According to weekly data from Petro-Logistics, total Russian exports of fuel oil from the Baltics and Black Sea were around 285,000 tonnes, bringing the total for the first three weeks of January to almost 700,000.
This compares to Petro-Logistics' assessment of some 900,000 tonnes exported from both regions in January.
Petro-Logistics did not separate the totals between the Baltic and the Black Sea.
Low sulphur fuel oil markets were effectively dead and buying interest was very hard to pin down.
One NWE refiner said prices had not changed and physical cargoes were worth around $100 fob NWE. Low sulphur swaps for March were talked at around $99 a tonne.
